title: Easy Chat
subtitle: Full Stack Web App
description: Easy Chat is a browser-based web messenger engineered for seamless, real-time communication without requiring heavy app downloads. The application features direct user-to-user messaging, inline media sharing, dynamic message controls (edit, replace, or delete), and full profile management. Built directly into the browser, it highlights clean front-end architecture, state management, and responsive UI design—delivering a fast, intuitive chat platform accessible on any device.
details:
Easy Chat: Architectural & Technical Deep Dive

Overview & Core Architecture

Easy Chat was built from the ground up to explore real-time web architecture without relying on heavy third-party UI framework state tools like Redux. Instead, state management across the application is engineered entirely around React’s Context API, keeping data flow predictable while keeping bundle sizes light.

Real-Time Infrastructure with WebSockets

To enable instant, low-latency communication between devices across the web, the platform relies on Socket.io. Every message transmission, status update, and session event is handled through custom event-driven WebSockets, maintaining persistent full-duplex connections across client browsers.

$$0$$

Creative Media Handling & Upload Pipelines

Handling images in real-time messaging often bloats payload sizes and strains server bandwidth. To solve this, Easy Chat delegates heavy media hosting to Cloudinary via client-side integration.

When a user attaches an image, the client compresses and uploads the asset directly to Cloudinary, receiving back a secure CDN URL. Instead of streaming heavy binary files through the WebSocket server, the app sends light text payloads containing the image reference and metadata. Special token markers in the message parser allow the front end to conditionally render full dynamic image components alongside standard text seamlessly.

$$1$$

$$2$$

Custom AI Integration & System Prompting

To enhance user interaction, Easy Chat includes an embedded AI assistant powered by Llama models via a custom API endpoint. Rather than implementing heavy context models, the system features a light UI tagging system that appends smart instruction prompts to user queries behind the scenes:

•Text Enhancement Tags: Modifies the outgoing payload to enforce detailed, natural language formatting from the model.

•Code Mode Tags: Appends strict structural directives to force the LLM to output clean, raw code blocks rather than conversational prose.

$$3$$

$$4$$

Session Management & Performance Optimizations

User persistence and seamless browsing were primary design goals. The front-end architecture implements a custom caching mechanism alongside browser session tracking. This ensures instant data loading during re-renders, minimizes redundant API fetches, and keeps active chat sessions synchronized across multiple browser tabs.

$$5$$

$$6$$

Lightweight Node.js Backend & In-Memory Data Strategy

The backend service is built on Node.js and hosted on Render. It orchestrates active user profiles, session validation, and real-time socket channels.

$$7$$

To maintain high performance during testing, the database architecture utilizes an in-memory SQL strategy. While runtime storage reset during server deployments presented unique challenges, it ensured zero storage latency for message routing and quick session handling.

$$8$$

Tech Stack

• Frontend: TypeScript • React 19 (Context API) • React Router v7 • Framer Motion • Bootstrap 5

• Backend: Node.js • Express v5 • Socket.io • JWT • bcrypt

• Database & Cloud: Turso (LibSQL/SQLite) • Cloudinary • Render • GitHub Pages

• Key Utilities: Axios • Browser-Image-Compression

title: Easy Park
subtitle: 3D / Animation
description: Easy Park is a 3D animated concept trailer for a mobile app designed to resolve urban parking gridlock. Built around a license plate scanning system that lets drivers instantly notify owners of blocked vehicles, the project was modeled, staged, and rendered in Blender to demonstrate motion design, camera composition, and app store promotional visualization.
details:
Easy Park: 3D Product Visualization & Animation Pipeline

Project Origin & Strategic Vision

Easy Park began as a business capstone project designed to address high-density urban parking gridlock in Armenia. To effectively communicate the business model to academic evaluators, potential investors, and government stakeholders—whose cooperation would be necessary for license plate database access—the project required more than a static pitch deck. 
The goal was to engineer a high-impact, 3D promotional trailer within a strict one-week production window, serving as an app store video showcase and proof of concept.

$$0$$

Environment Staging & Scene Optimization

Built for high-fidelity visual output rather than real-time game performance, the complete 3D environment contained over 1,861,000 triangles. To maintain rapid production velocity without reinventing base assets, existing 3D models were integrated, restructured, and optimized for the scene.

• Shader & Material Reconstruction: Imported assets were stripped of broken dependencies and rebuilt. Materials were re-linked, adjusted, and blended using custom procedural shaders inside

• Blender's Shader Editor.Scene Clean-up: Extravagant vehicle details were pruned, and materials were unified to establish a consistent, realistic urban aesthetic across the entire set.

$$1$$

$$2$$

Cinematic Camera Work & Motion Tracking

To give the trailer the polished feel of a commercial advertisement, the camera animation relied heavily on dynamic lenses, depth-of-field manipulation, and motion constraints. 

• Dynamic Lens Selection: Focal lengths were altered continuously throughout the sequence—ranging from wide 27mm environmental framing to tight 136mm telephoto tracking shots—to direct viewer attention.

• Cinematic Focus & Motion Tracking: 
Cameras were parented to character joint rigs and vehicle paths, utilizing continuous depth-of-field tracking to switch focus between the driver, the vehicle, and the mobile UI in real time.

$$3$$

$$4$$

Creative UI Compositing & Handheld Simulation

Rather than building complex in-engine 3D interface animations, a hybrid screen-mapping workflow was executed:

1: Transparent UI Masking: The mobile device’s viewport screen was modeled with a transparent camera region inside the UI overlay.

2: Video Texture Mapping: Pre-recorded footage was mapped directly as an animated material texture onto the 3D phone screen inside Blender.

3: Micro-Shake Simulation: Subtle procedural noise and camera shake were keyframed into the 3D phone rig to simulate organic handheld movement, ensuring the digital UI felt naturally embedded in the physical scene.

$$5$$

$$6$$

Lighting, Cycles Rendering & Post-Production

To achieve realistic outdoor lighting, the scene combined HDRI environment maps with a directional Sun Light and supplemental 3-point studio lighting for character keying.

• Render Engine: Rendered entirely in Cycles at 1080p / 24 fps to ensure physical light transport, glass refraction, and accurate vehicle paint reflections.

• Editorial & Post-Processing: Final render passes were exported from Blender into external video editing software for final color grading, pacing edits, audio synchronization, and post-effects.

$$7$$

title: HK416
subtitle: 3D / Animation
description: A detailed 3D model of a modern assault rifle inspired by the HK416 platform, created as a high-fidelity digital asset for visualization and animation purposes. It includes multiple visualization variants such as solid, textured, UV-mapped, and topology-focused versions, making it suitable for both rendering and study of structure and form.
details: The model was created in Blender and consists of 40,991 triangles. It includes a fully rigged bone system designed to simulate realistic firearm mechanics, allowing for full animation of components such as the trigger and other movable parts. The asset was built with clean topology and UV mapping to support different rendering workflows, including textured and non-textured (solid) visual modes. It is optimized for animation, with a fully controllable rig that allows realistic motion simulation of firearm operation within 3D environments.

title: Thomas
subtitle: 3D / Animation
description: A high-quality 3D game character meticulously handcrafted in Blender. This project features two optimized versions of a realistic human model, designed for seamless integration into game engines. By combining professional sculpting techniques with a custom hair-card system and hybrid texturing, the model achieves a balance of high-fidelity realism and performance-ready optimization.
details: A meticulously handcrafted 3D game character created entirely within Blender, featuring two optimized versions with 91,626 and 71,698 triangles respectively. The character features a high-fidelity grooming system for the hair, beard, mustache, and eyebrows, developed by converting splines and curves into meshes with rendered hair cards rather than utilizing traditional hair strips. The texturing is a hybrid of procedural methods and hand-adjusted reference imagery; specifically, the jeans utilize actual textures while items like the hoodie, shorts, and shoes utilize atlas textures for materials like cotton and rubber. The skin is reconstructed from a real 3D photo-scan, using procedural texturing to maintain high-resolution color variation. For added realism, the eyes are built with translucent objects that realistically bend light. All assets are fully baked into textures, ensuring the model is completely portable and functional in any software or game engine outside of Blender.
